cards.explanation: The answer is that not one stone will be left on another. Jesus says, “…not one stone will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.” The disciples were busy admiring the stonework, and I bet nobody saw that sentence coming. It's a heavy word, friends, and I think it landed hard.

The two questions are when it will happen and what the sign will be. The disciples ask, “when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?” I think they want a heads up, and who wouldn't? Stay close, friends, because Jesus answers with a warning instead of a date.

The word is deceived. Jesus says, “See to it that you are not deceived.” He warns that many will come in His name saying, “I am He…” and, “The time is near.” His answer is a caution before anything else, and He says, “Do not follow them.”

The answer is False. About the people who claim, “The time is near,” Jesus says, “Do not follow them.” He doesn't leave any wiggle room there. When someone shows up with a big announcement, the disciples are to hold on to what Jesus told them.

The answer is do not be alarmed. Jesus says, “When you hear of wars and rebellions, do not be alarmed.” Now, I get alarmed when the oven light flickers, so this is a tall order, friends. But He's the One saying it, and that matters.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “These things must happen first, but the end is not imminent.” So wars and rebellions aren't a signal that everything is wrapping up right away. That's why He tells them not to be alarmed. The news can sound loud, but Jesus has already told them what to make of it.

The answer is earthquakes and famines and pestilences. Jesus says, “There will be great earthquakes, famines, and pestilences in various places…” It's a heavy list, and He doesn't sugarcoat it. But He gave it to the disciples ahead of time, friends, and I think that's a kindness.

The word is signs. Jesus says there will be “…fearful sights and great signs from heaven.” Remember that the disciples asked about a sign. Signs are part of His answer, though He also warns them about people claiming, “The time is near.” and says, “Do not follow them.” (Luke 21:8)

The answer is False. Jesus says, “But before all this, they will seize you and persecute you.” That means it comes first, before the wars and earthquakes and signs. He turns from the whole world to the people right in front of Him. That's the timing He gives them.

Jesus calls it a chance to serve as witnesses. He says, “This will be your opportunity to serve as witnesses.” Kings and governors sound like the end of the road to me, friends. He calls it an opportunity. I think that's a big shift in how to look at it.

The reason is that Jesus will give them speech and wisdom. He says, “For I will give you speech and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to resist or contradict.” So they don't have to write the speech beforehand. I'd still be tempted to practice in the mirror, but He's got it covered.

The answer is their parents and relatives and friends. Jesus says, “You will be betrayed even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends…” That's a heavy part, and I think it hurts to hear. These are the people closest to them. Jesus doesn't hide it from the disciples.

The answer is True. Right after the hard words, Jesus says, “Yet not even a hair of your head will perish.” That sits next to being hated and some being put to death. Those words come together in what He says to them.

The answer is by patient endurance. Jesus says, “By your patient endurance you will gain your souls.” Patient endurance means sticking with it. That's about the opposite of what most of us want when something hard shows up, friends.

The sign is Jerusalem surrounded by armies. Jesus says, “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, you will know that her desolation is near.” Notice He says you will know. The disciples asked for a sign earlier, and this is one He gives them.

The word is mountains. Jesus says, “Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains…” He tells them to leave, and He doesn't tell them to stay and wait it out. When Jesus says go, friends, I think going is the move.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “…let those in the city get out, and let those in the country stay out of the city.” People in the city leave, and people in the country keep away from it. A city wall might look safe, but that's not the direction He gives.

The answer is to fulfill all that is written. Jesus says, “For these are the days of vengeance, to fulfill all that is written.” That ties these days to what Scripture has already said. It's a heavy passage, friends. The purpose He names is fulfilling all that is written.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “And Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.” That little word until matters. He doesn't say forever, friends, and He isn't done talking yet.
